idiom_name: Ktor plugin pipeline (createApplicationPlugin) or Spring HandlerInterceptor
implementation_notes: In Kotlin the shared security sequence is a framework interception point: a Ktor plugin installed on the application - or on a route subtree - runs its onCall and intercept phases before the handler, and Spring's HandlerInterceptor (or OncePerRequestFilter) plays the same role in a Boot application. Either way the base-action structure disappears: one installed plugin or interceptor holds the sequence and handlers stay business-only. Routing itself is a plugin in Ktor, so installation scope and order are part of the security contract.
pitfalls: Plugins apply globally unless installed on a route subtree, and route-level installation overrides the global configuration; install scope and order decide what is checked.
Handlers that branch out of the ordinary pipeline (WebSockets, SSE, raw streams) may not cross the same plugin stage; verify each transport.
Blocking calls inside onCall block the event loop; move blocking work to an appropriate dispatcher.
